metadata.title: Fictional FO 13
metadata.systemPrompt: Write only fictional reports in plain ASCII English. Never use tools or refer to any real project, person, or conversation. Follow the requested length.

item.text: Write a fictional status report for Project Pebble 13, a pretend internal library-booking trial. Total length: 6500 to 8500 ASCII characters, never more than 9000. Use SIX dated entries, around 1100 characters each; do not add extra entries. Describe a pretend pilot scope, an earlier missing cancellation path, its repair and checks, a remaining fictional limitation, and a current Captain decision about starting the pretend trial. If postponed, the trial does not start. All facts and names must be fictional. Include concrete mundane test notes to reach at least 6500 characters, then stop after entry six. No tools, headings outside the entries or setup commentary.

2026-10-02

Project Pebble 13 entered pilot phase with Rosewood Library and three satellite branches this week. The scope covers reserving physical materials up to 14 days in advance, with holds placed against the branch inventory system. Pilot duration is 4 weeks, with 25 volunteer staff across all branches. Hardware footprint is one shared tablet per branch, phoned home to a central booking service running on Maroon infrastructure. Staff sign in with printed badge codes scanned by barcode reader; no authentication backend needed for this trial. Intake survey showed 18 staff confident with form entry, 7 uncertain. We ran one 90-minute hands-on with the tablet interface at each branch, covering the happy path: search, select copy, enter patron name, choose pickup date. No data was retained after that session. The pilot starts this Friday. All staff have printed one-page quick-reference cards showing the five-step reservation flow and the phone number to call if something breaks.

2026-10-08

On Monday morning, second day of live use, branch manager at Rosewood called to report staff could not cancel a reservation placed in error. A patron had booked a copy of "Tides of Winter" for Oct 15, but the patron called back five minutes later asking to cancel. Staff found no way to mark a reservation as cancelled or delete it from the tablet interface. Checking the stored records, the reservation was visible in the service logs but no UI element existed to modify it. We took the branch offline, advised the patron's card would be removed from the hold list manually via spreadsheet, and opened an investigation. This delayed our confidence briefing with the branch managers by two hours. The issue was categorized as P1 due to staff having no path to correct mistakes, which is a baseline failure mode for any booking system.

2026-10-09

Root cause analysis: the pilot build included a reservation-creation flow but did not include any path to view or cancel existing reservations. The reservation list existed in the database but was never exposed to the tablet UI. The Pebble 13 feature roadmap had cancellation flagged for phase two, expected in December, so it was cut from the pilot scope in the August design review. However, the pilot brief to staff did not call out this gap, creating an expectation that all standard patron requests could be handled. We prepared a two-part fix: first, a read-only view showing all active reservations for the branch, accessible from the main screen by button press, and second, a cancel button on each reservation that marks it cancelled in the database without deleting the record. The fix was coded and tested in isolation on Wednesday afternoon. Total changes: 47 lines added to the tablet app, 12 lines added to the service layer to accept the cancellation request.

2026-10-10

Fix deployed to all four branch tablets at 09:15 on Thursday morning. First test: created a test reservation under the name "Morgan Vale" for "Cryptic Signals" on Oct 12, then immediately pressed the cancel button from the reservation list. The reservation status changed from "active" to "cancelled" in under 2 seconds. We repeated this flow 12 times with different material titles and dates to rule out timing issues or data corruption. Each cancellation succeeded. Staff at each branch were called during lunch break, shown the new button location on the tablet, and did a walkthrough: create a dummy reservation (using staff member name), view it in the list, cancel it. All four branches confirmed the button worked and the cancellation appeared on their screen. Rosewood staff tested with 8 cancellations of real patron holds over the next two hours, and all cancellations were recorded correctly in the logs. No errors in the system event stream.

2026-10-15

Extended testing over the past five days covered edge cases and concurrent access. We created reservations under names with accented characters, apostrophes, and names longer than 30 characters; all cancelled cleanly. We tested the scenario where a staff member creates a reservation, another staff member at a different branch views the full list, and the first staff member cancels that same reservation. The cancellation propagated to all views within 3 seconds. We tested cancelling the same reservation twice in rapid succession (simulating a network retry); the second attempt correctly returned "already cancelled" instead of crashing. We tested power-off scenarios: if the tablet lost connectivity after clicking cancel but before the response returned, the button stayed disabled for 30 seconds, then re-enabled and showed the correct cancelled status when the staff member refreshed the list. One limitation remains: if a patron calls to cancel but the original reservation was placed at a different branch, staff cannot view or cancel it remotely. They must call Rosewood to request the cancellation on their behalf. This was identified as out of scope for the pilot but should be captured as a follow-up item.

2026-10-22

Pilot is now in week three of four. Total reservations placed across all branches: 287. Cancellations initiated by staff via the new interface: 31. Zero errors or data loss events in the cancellation path. Staff confidence survey administered on Tuesday shows 24 of 25 staff now rate the system as "usable" or "usable with help"; only one staff member (Northside branch) remains neutral, citing occasional tablet slowness during peak morning hours. Captain has called a go-no-go meeting for Friday afternoon to decide whether to extend the trial by six weeks or to merge Pebble 13 into standard operations beginning November 5. The decision hinges on whether the cross-branch remote cancellation limitation is acceptable for launch or whether it blocks rollout. Three satellite branches want the feature before expansion; Rosewood branch manager believes the current flow is sufficient if documented clearly. Maroon infrastructure team has signaled capacity to absorb the service into production ops if authorized. All test data has been archived. No decision yet on Captain's position. Update expected by end of week.
